acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Sara and Ethan have been dating for 10 months. They see each other at least once a week, text pretty much every day, and have been there for each other through hard times. But they refuse to have the “what are we?” conversation. So what gives? Guest host Tobin Low looks into it.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: Last week, when Temporary Protected Status, also known as TPS, was cut off for Haitian immigrants, some 300,000 people had their lives upended. Marie, a Certified Nursing Assistant in Boston, was one of them. Producer Chana Joffe-Walt spent time last week with Marie as she tried to figure out exactly when her very last day on the job would be.
acts.title: Last Shift

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Comedian Janet McNamara was walking off stage 15 years ago when the club owner asked, “Hey, have you ever been tested for autism?” No one had ever asked her this before, so Janet decided to look into it.
To see Janet live, check out her website and her special, “ Not Smart Enough.”
acts.title: Diagnose Me, Maybe?

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc:
When you get down to it, labels are just our way of pointing out what we think is remarkable about other people. That’s Alfred Jung Lee’s argument. He’s been thinking a lot about how we describe each other, especially as he tries to describe his wife, who passed away from cancer.
This essay originally ran in The Believer.
acts.credits: By Alfred Jung Lee; Produced by Diane Wu

songs.t: You Can’t Judge a Book by the Cover

acts.title: The Last Description
